title: Touring with the Alabama and Georgia Minstrels at 16 or 17
summary: When minstrel shows came through town they hired him on trombone; Edgar Battle was in the shows and trumpeter Harry White could play jazz.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: See, but I -- later years, when I was about 16, 17, I got on the circuit, the shows -- see, I was with Alabama too, but I was just remembering one time (inaudible) I was with that and the Alabama Minstrel and the Georgia Minstrel.
You told Sonny that already, did you?
No, I didn't tell that because I forgot about it.
How come you went with the minstrel shows then? I mean, who --
Because the shows come through town and
I would be playing trombone and I was good and they wanted me.
And go out and tour with them?
Those minstrel shows, would you drum up business up front before the show?
Was there anybody else in the bands that you knew then in those minstrel shows?
Yeah, Battle was in the shows all the time.
And we would know somebody else in there who could play and they had some trumpet players in there that could play jazz, like a fella named Harry White out in Detroit.
Could play jazz, too, you know, could play solo work. But the jazz wasn't like it is today, you know, he just --
I don't know who I could say he played like. But he could play a few notes in jazz (inaudible) had some bluesy licks, you know (inaudible) trombone (inaudible).
Well, of course, trombone, I mean, that fitted right in with minstrel shows and that because it carries and everything.
